newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends 96 tightly mixed, March rebounds.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends 96 tightly mixed, March rebounds.

text.p: London cocoa futures finished the year on a mixed note with benchmark March bouncing to the plus column after a sharp fall on Monday.
Traders said the March advance reflected some sympathetic buying in London on New York's gains.
New York prices propelled higher on buying led by the weakness of the dollar against the sterling.
But dealings were slow in the abbreviated afternoon session ahead of Wednesday's New Year holiday. Trading resumes on Thursday.
The March position dipped early in the day to test a crucial 880 stg support on producer selling inspired by firmer sterling.
But it managed to crawl back in the afternoon to finish 1996 three stg up at 890 stg a tonne.
The contract had dropped to 16-month-lows of 878 stg at one stage on Monday but managed to close above 880 support. Immediate resistance is pegged at 900.
Traders also noted the narrowing of nearby spreads with the bids being raised.
March/May spread and May/July spread eased by three and two stg to 15 stg each. Expired December was untraded.
Fundamentally, all eyes were set on West African crop arrivals which would help gauge the size of 1996/97 harvest.
Preliminary forecasts put crop from key grower Ivory Coast at around 1.0 million tonnes but traders said they hoped to get a clearer crop picture by the New Year.
